title: Correlated Shared State Observed Without a Consistent Snapshot
pattern: Related shared values whose combined state must satisfy an invariant are updated or read through separate operations that allow a concurrent reader to observe values from different logical versions.
why_bad: Individually valid values can form an impossible combined snapshot, such as account balances straddling a transfer or a new `meas_1` paired with an old `meas_2`, leaving readers fatally confused and violating the object's transactional integrity invariants. Unsynchronized plain access may also be a data race under the relevant language model; individually atomic fields do not by themselves provide a multi-field snapshot.
detection: Establish a writer, a potentially concurrent reader, correlated values, and a requirement to observe one coherent version. Inspect the update routine and the full multi-value read, including reads through separately locking getters, per-field atomics, or a mutable class exposing multiple getters. Report missing coordination across the entire logical update/read (no common lock, atomic snapshot, RCU boundary, or transaction spanning all of it), even where each individual access is synchronized. Do not infer concurrency from sequential assignments under Rust's exclusive `&mut` access alone.
source: *1701.00854v6.pdf* by Paul McKenney (Section 13.5.4, "Correlated Fields"); Martin Fowler (PEEAA) Ch 15, Alex Petrov Ch 5; [The Addison-Wesley signature series] Martin Fowler - PEAA, p. 235 [235].
